title: Order-quality evaluation harness and customer benchmark ingestion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible evaluation harness for rank-order quality that can run NDCG and MRR metrics on both synthetic and customer-supplied prompt sets, instrumented end-to-end across the embeddings + reranking endpoint stack. Deliverables: (1) ingestion pipeline for customer prompt sets with PII-safe anonymization and schema validation, (2) deterministic eval runner supporting offline and live (canary/A-B) modes, (3) telemetry hooks that surface NDCG/MRR deltas and statistical significance in Console dashboards, and (4) integration tests and a baseline benchmark suite for embedding dot-product vs hybrid scoring models.
acceptance_criteria: Customer prompt ingestion supports CSV/JSONL with schema mapping and automatic anonymization (no raw PII persisted)
Eval runner computes ndcg@10 and mrr@10 with deterministic tie-breaking and provides per-query and aggregated outputs
Console displays NDCG/MRR time series and experiment deltas with p-value calculation for AB comparisons
A/B hook exists: traffic split, rollback thresholds (ndcg delta <= -0.02 and p < 0.05), and automated rollback playbook
Perf budget: p95 latency for reranker <= 12ms at batch size 16 (baseline hardware) and regression tests to detect >5% throughput degradation
End-to-end integration tests and a reproducible baseline benchmark dataset checked into infra repo
decisions: Use ndcg@10 and mrr@10 as primary quality metrics because product search customers care about top-K ordering
Deterministic tie-breaking: use stable document id ordering to ensure eval reproducibility across runs
Anonymization approach: hash tokens and drop free-form PII fields; store only normalized query and label enums
Stat test: two-sided permutation test for significance (works with small n and non-normal distributions)
Default AB rollback threshold: ndcg drop <= -0.02 with p < 0.05 (configurable per experiment)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local runner with synthetic promptsets and unit tests
Phase 1 (internal canary): run on 5% of internal traffic with metric collection and compare against baseline for 48h
Phase 2 (customer pilot): allow opt-in customer promptset ingestion and run A/B with 10-20% traffic
Phase 3 (GA): expose as Console experiment template with safety limits and auto-rollback
